inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K consolidated cash flow statement, 'Stock-based compensation' add-back $955M (ABBV_Annual_FY2025.txt:5286); AbbVie publishes no combined equity-award figure and does not break out net-share-settlement tax withholding (it sits inside financing 'Other, net'), so the add-back is used as the combined figure. 9M-2026 run-rate $770M on $49.4B revenue = 1.56% of revenue, unchanged.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 'Purchases of treasury stock' $980M (10-K:5314); 9M-2026 $1,503M (10-Q:3197). Buybacks exceed SBC-driven issuance, so the flat share count is funded, not a convention. Dividends ($11.7B FY2025, $1.73/qtr from Feb-2026) are the main return channel and are not modelled separately: they come out of the same owner FCF.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T21:01:45Z regular close (Friday); valuation written Sunday 2026-11-08, no after-hours print involved
inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares, Q3-2026 10-Q (basic 1,769M + 3M dilutive RSU/option effect, two-class method; 10-Q:3278-3280). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; buybacks ($1.0-1.5B/yr) more than absorb grant dilution.
inputs.net_debt_note: Q3-2026 balance sheet: current portion of LTD $8,673M + long-term debt $72,230M = $80,903M gross (finance leases included in those captions, no short-term borrowings/CP outstanding); cash $10,774M. Debt rose ~$10B in 2026 because $9.0B of senior notes (4.50%-6.00%) were issued in Aug-2026 to fund the $10.5B Apogee acquisition. Contingent consideration liabilities (Skyrizi royalty to Boehringer Ingelheim, $25.4B fair value at FY2025) are NOT added to net debt: the royalty cash is charged inside the EBITDA margin path instead (charge once). Operating lease liabilities ($924M) are left in the flows, not in net debt.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment A: operating lease cost stays inside EBITDA (it is in COGS/SG&A), lease liabilities excluded from net debt. Immaterial either way ($924M on $81B debt).
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interest earns $7-10M/yr; ignored as immaterial (no bridge deduction, flows not reduced).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. 10y UST ~4.2%, ERP 5.0%, observed beta ~0.6 gives cost of equity ~7.2%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (Aug-2026 notes priced 4.50%-6.00%), ~4.0% after tax; market-value weights ~87/13 give CAPM WACC ~6.8%. A 7.5% WACC is used across all three scenarios: the low measured beta reflects index-defensive trading, not the policy (MFN, IRA negotiation) and 2033 Skyrizi/Rinvoq LOE risk that sits in these specific flows, and the house convention is to charge pharma no lower than 7.5%. Scenario risk is carried in the driver paths and weights, not in per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF, routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md as a US operating company (large-cap pharma). First valuation of ABBV; no prior DCF or memory entry. FOUR ADJUSTMENTS DEFINE THE HOUSE BASE AND ALL ARE DELIBERATE. (1) EBITDA is defined as operating earnings + depreciation + intangible amortisation + impairments + acquired IPR&D + SBC, MINUS the cash paid on contingent consideration (the Skyrizi royalty to Boehringer: $2,865M FY2025, $2,717M 9M-2026, ~16% of Skyrizi sales). That royalty never touches the P&L (it is a liability settlement; the P&L shows only fair-value remeasurement in Other expense), so sell-side 'adjusted' earnings exclude it entirely; it is nonetheless a cash cost of ~4.7% of group revenue that scales with the biggest product. FY2025 on this definition: $27,167M = 44.4%; 9M-2026: 43.9% (45.4% ex one-off Apogee cash-settled awards and integration costs). (2) D&A in the build is DEPRECIATION ONLY (~1.25% of revenue). The $7.4B/yr intangible amortisation (Allergan) is non-cash and, with little tax basis, essentially non-deductible (the P&L carries a deferred-tax benefit for it, cash tax does not), so including it would manufacture a ~$1.5B/yr phantom tax shield that runs off as it amortises. (3) capex_pct bundles PP&E capex (2.0% FY2025, rising toward 2.4% with the announced US manufacturing build-out) with a NORMALISED business-development charge of 5.0% of revenue (base) for acquired IPR&D/milestones and bolt-on pipeline acquisitions. Reported OCF excludes these payments (they are investing cash flows: $5.2B IPR&D in FY2025, $10.5B Apogee in 2026, $17.5B ImmunoGen+Cerevel in 2024), yet a pharma cannot sustain revenue without them. FY2021-25 expensed IPR&D averaged 3.6% of revenue; adding business combinations lifts the 2024-26 actual spend to ~15% of revenue. 5% is therefore generous to the company and consistent with crediting only modest pipeline-driven growth in the base path. (4) Cash tax is applied to EBIT = EBITDA - SBC - depreciation on an UNLEVERED basis: FY2025 cash taxes $3,626M plus the ~$0.6B interest tax shield embedded in them is 16.6% of that EBIT (FY2024 ~21%, FY2023 ~22% with IRS settlement effects); the adjusted ETR guided ~15.5-16.5% rises with Pillar Two and the Jan-2026 US pricing/manufacturing agreement, so the base ramps 17% -> 19%. CONSEQUENCE: house owner FCF for FY2025 after these adjustments is ~$16.0B unlevered (~26% margin) against ~$18.8B of adjusted net income and $17.8B reported FCF; the gap is the royalty plus normalised BD, and it is the main reason the house value sits well below the market price. last_fcf follows the contract (reported FCF - SBC - interest income = $16,595M, a levered figure) and is NOT the year-0 of the projection; the projection starts from the component build. Interest income ($266M) is stripped per contract although net debt is large; it is immaterial at 0.4% of revenue. Horizon is 10 years (FY2026-FY2035) so that the 2033 Skyrizi/Rinvoq loss of exclusivity falls inside the explicit period in every scenario rather than being hidden in the terminal multiple.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Management's stated high-single-digit revenue CAGR through 2029 (Skyrizi+Rinvoq >$31B by 2027 and still compounding 20%+ in 9M-2026), haircut to 6% as the mid-horizon base rate; cross-checked against the 5-yr revenue CAGR of 5.95% (FY2020-FY2025). Equity CAGR is unusable (book equity negative: -$3,270M FY2025) and GAAP EPS is noise (IPR&D, contingent-consideration remeasurement, impairments), so neither is the primary input.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR undefined (negative shareholders' equity after Allergan-era buybacks and dividends); GAAP EPS 3-yr CAGR -29% diverges from revenue +1.75% by far more than 30% because FY2025 GAAP earnings carry $5.0B acquired IPR&D and $6.5B contingent-consideration remeasurement. Growth selection therefore rests on revenue guidance and product-level trends, flagged for review.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY2020 ~15,864 (interest income estimated ~175 from 9M-2020 163; FY2022 10-K not in folder), FY2021 21,259, FY2022 23,391, FY2023 20,775, FY2024 16,273, FY2025 16,595. The 5-yr revenue CAGR is flattered by Allergan contributing only 7 months to FY2020; the 3-yr CAGR (1.75%) is the Humira cliff (US Humira $12.2B in 2023 -> $3.1B in 2025) nearly fully offset by Skyrizi/Rinvoq (+$14.1B over the same period). SBC grew 4.9%/yr FY2020-25 while owner FCF was flat, so a rising slice of reported cash generation is being paid in stock, though at 1.56% of revenue it remains small by US standards. Owner FCF FY2023-25 is also depressed relative to FY2021-22 by contingent-consideration payments moving into operating cash flow ($0.9B FY2023 -> $2.9B FY2025) as Skyrizi scaled.

base.growth_note: FY2026 +10% matches the 9M-2026 run-rate (+10.9%, Q3 +10.3%; FY2026 ~$67.3B). Deceleration to mid-single digits by 2030 as Skyrizi/Rinvoq mature, IRA negotiated prices hit Imbruvica (2026), Vraylar/Linzess (2027), Botox (2028) and the Jan-2026 US pricing agreement bites. FY2033-34 flat-to-negative for the start of Skyrizi/Rinvoq US biosimilar/generic entry, partly offset by pipeline (tavapadon, Emrelis, Elahere, Apogee IL-13, obesity). Recovery to 2% in FY2035 and terminal 2%.
base.margin_note: EBITDA (pre-SBC, after Skyrizi royalty cash, before IPR&D) 44.4% FY2025 / ~45.4% 9M-2026 ex one-offs. Operating leverage from Humira erosion ending and Skyrizi/Rinvoq scale lifts it to 46.5% by FY2029, with the rising royalty bill (Skyrizi share of revenue climbing) absorbing part of the gain; eases to 45.5% as LOE begins.
base.capex_note: PP&E 2.0% rising to 2.4% (US API facility, Massachusetts biologics expansion, Arizona device plant) plus 5.0% normalised business development; see inputs.notes.
base.tax_note: Unlevered cash tax on EBIT (EBITDA - SBC - depreciation): 16.6% FY2025 actual, ramped to 19% for Pillar Two and a larger US income mix under the Jan-2026 manufacturing/pricing agreement.
base.wc_note: Growth consumes working capital at AbbVie: receivables and inventory build; FY2025 -33% of the revenue increase, 9M-2026 -19%. -15% is used (negative capture: growth is a cash drain).
base.terminal_note: Cap lowered 18x -> 16x in the sanity fix pass (2026-11-08): the terminal year is post-2033 Skyrizi/Rinvoq LOE, so the method's lower cap for structurally slower businesses applies; Gordon at 7.5%/2% (18.5x) therefore does not bind.

bull.note: Pipeline replaces the 2033 LOE with no revenue dip: BD charge 4% of revenue (closer to the FY2021-25 expensed-IPR&D average), margins reach 48.5%, tax settles at 18%.
bull.terminal_note: Cap 20x -> 18x in the sanity fix pass; even with the pipeline replacing the LOE, a mature pharma does not sustain a 20x owner-FCF exit.

bear.note: MFN/reference pricing spreads beyond the Jan-2026 agreement, IRA takes Botox in 2028, Skyrizi/Rinvoq lose exclusivity in 2033 with the pipeline (obesity, Apogee, neuroscience) under-delivering; BD spend rises to 6% of revenue to backfill while margins compress. Terminal cap 14x for an ex-growth pharma.
bear.terminal_note: Cap 14x -> 12x in the sanity fix pass: ex-growth pharma after an unreplaced LOE.

scenario_narratives.base: Skyrizi ($17.6B FY2025, +50%; 9M-2026 +26%) and Rinvoq ($8.3B, +39%; 9M-2026 +24%) have already replaced Humira ($14.4B in 2023 -> $4.5B in 2025 -> ~$2.8B run-rate), so the Humira cliff is behind the company and FY2026 grows ~10%. The base case takes management's high-single-digit CAGR through 2029 and decelerates it as the two immunology franchises mature, IRA-negotiated prices arrive (Imbruvica 2026, Vraylar/Linzess 2027, Botox 2028) and the Jan-2026 US pricing/manufacturing agreement trades price concessions for tariff and MFN exemptions. Aesthetics (Botox Cosmetic -4%, Juvederm -15% in 2025) stays soft; neuroscience (Vraylar, Botox Therapeutic, Ubrelvy, Qulipta, Vyalev, tavapadon) and oncology (Venclexta, Elahere, Emrelis) grow but cannot match immunology's scale. The explicit period runs to FY2035 so the 2033 Skyrizi/Rinvoq LOE is modelled (flat/-1% years) rather than capitalised away; pipeline replacement is credited only to the extent the 5%-of-revenue BD charge pays for it. Two costs the street ignores are charged in full: the ~16% Skyrizi royalty paid to Boehringer Ingelheim through contingent consideration ($2.9B in FY2025, growing with the product) and a normalised business-development spend in lieu of the IPR&D/acquisition cash that sits outside reported FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: Skyrizi and Rinvoq keep compounding into new indications (IBD, GCA, alopecia, vitiligo, HS) and together exceed $35B before 2030; the Apogee IL-13 franchise, tavapadon in Parkinson's, Emrelis and the amylin/obesity program (Gubra) deliver so that the 2033 LOE is a plateau rather than a dip; aesthetics recovers with the consumer; margins reach 48.5% as the Allergan integration and Humira drag are fully lapped; BD stays at the historical ~4% of revenue; the Jan-2026 agreement caps rather than escalates US pricing risk. Terminal growth 2.5%, cap 20x.
scenario_narratives.bear: US drug-pricing policy escalates beyond the current agreement (MFN benchmarks spread to commercial payers, Medicaid pricing concessions widen), Botox's 2028 IRA price and PBM formulary pressure cut neuroscience and aesthetics, and when Skyrizi/Rinvoq biosimilars and generics arrive in 2033 the pipeline has not produced a franchise of comparable size, so revenue falls 5-7%/yr for two years while R&D and BD spend rise to 6% of revenue to backfill. The Boehringer royalty keeps scaling with Skyrizi until LOE, so margin compression is amplified. Net debt of $70B (plus a $25B royalty liability) is serviced but constrains buybacks; the dividend is maintained. Terminal growth 1%, cap 14x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 20%: the bear axis is a dated, known event (2033 Skyrizi/Rinvoq LOE) compounded by an active US pricing-policy regime, and AbbVie carries $70B of net debt against negative book equity, so a weak pipeline outcome has little balance-sheet cushion. Bull cut from 35% to 30%: it needs several independent things to go right (obesity entry, Apogee's late-stage IL-13 asset, neuroscience launches, benign policy) rather than one. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: AbbVie is valued as a stream of owner cash flow after every cost that actually leaves the company: SBC, the Boehringer royalty on Skyrizi (paid through contingent consideration and invisible to adjusted EPS), and a normalised business-development spend standing in for the IPR&D and bolt-on acquisition cash that reported FCF excludes. Intangible amortisation is ignored as non-cash and largely non-deductible, so no phantom tax shield is capitalised. The horizon is extended to ten years so the 2033 immunology LOE is in the explicit period. The result is a house value substantially below the market price; the gap is almost entirely explained by the street capitalising adjusted earnings that exclude the royalty and treat acquisitions as free. Terminal caps were tightened to 16x/18x/12x in the sanity fix pass; see sanity_check.
key_risks_to_valuation: Skyrizi/Rinvoq loss of exclusivity (~2033): the base assumes a two-year flat/-1% dip with partial pipeline offset; the bear a -12% two-year decline. Patent-settlement timing could move the cliff either way.

US drug pricing: IRA negotiated prices (Imbruvica 2026, Vraylar/Linzess 2027, Botox 2028), the Jan-2026 three-year MFN/tariff agreement, and PBM leverage. Each further selection or policy extension is a direct hit to the growth path.

Normalised BD charge (5% of revenue): actual 2024-26 IPR&D plus acquisitions ran ~15% of revenue. If that pace is the true sustaining cost, the base overstates value; if BD is genuinely growth capex that the growth path under-credits, it understates it.

Boehringer royalty: charged at ~16% of Skyrizi sales for the full horizon via the EBITDA margin; the contingent-consideration liability ($25.4B) is not separately deducted. Double-counting is avoided but the royalty's end date is uncertain ('longer estimated royalty period' in the FY2025 10-K).
Tax: adjusted ETR ~16% today; Pillar Two, the OBBBA international changes and a larger US manufacturing footprint could move the cash rate either way. Each 1pp is roughly $4-5/share.

Leverage: $81B gross debt, $70B net, $9B added in 2026 for Apogee; refinancing at 4.5-6.0% versus Allergan-era 2-3% coupons raises interest cost (this is a WACC/cost-of-debt effect in an unlevered DCF, but constrains capital returns).
Terminal value: at 7.5% WACC and 2% growth the 18x cap binds; the terminal share of value is high, so the sensitivity grid should be read alongside the headline.
valuation_philosophy.sanity_check: Multiples sanity check tripped on implied GAAP P/E (100x vs a 47x ten-year average, itself inflated by trough-GAAP FY2023-25). GAAP EPS at AbbVie is not an earnings measure the DCF can be reconciled to: $7.4B of non-cash Allergan amortisation, $6.5B of Skyrizi royalty-liability remeasurement and $5.0B of expensed IPR&D take FY2025 GAAP EPS to $2.37 against ~$10.6 adjusted. The one fix applied was to lower the terminal cap multiples (base 18x->16x, bull 20x->18x, bear 14x->12x) because the terminal year is post-2033 LOE and the method prescribes 12-15x for structurally slower businesses; this took the weighted IV down ~8%. No WACC premium or growth cap was added: the growth paths are guidance-anchored and risk is already charged once through scenario weights. Read the P/E figure on the dashboard as a GAAP artefact; the cash-based multiples (price/owner-FCF, price/adjusted EPS) are the ones that describe this valuation.

fix_applied: 2026-11-08 sanity fix pass (single): terminal_cap_multiple lowered base 18->16, bull 20->18, bear 14->12. Rationale: terminal year FY2035 is post-Skyrizi/Rinvoq LOE, a structurally slower pharma, for which owner-fcf.md prescribes a 12-15x range; the prior 18x base let Gordon (18.5x at 7.5%/2%) nearly bind. No WACC premium added (risk is carried in scenario paths and weights, charged once); growth paths unchanged (guidance-anchored).
sanity_trip_context: Trip: implied P/E 100.1x vs 2x the 10-yr GAAP-P/E average (47.2x). The denominator is GAAP EPS ($2.37 FY2025) depressed by $7.4B non-cash intangible amortisation, $6.5B contingent-consideration remeasurement and $5.0B acquired IPR&D; the 10-yr average itself is inflated by FY2023-25 trough-GAAP years (66x/93x/124x). On cash measures the weighted IV is ~20x FY2026 levered owner FCF and ~13x adjusted FY2026 EPS, and it sits 35% below the market price (which trades at ~150x GAAP EPS). The P/E rule is therefore a weak gauge for ABBV; the fix applied is a method-grounded tightening of the terminal cap, not a concession that the valuation was too high relative to GAAP earnings.

implied_multiples_after_fix.note: Weighted IV 174.17 after the terminal-cap fix (was 188.96; implied P/E 100.1x before). P/E bound is 2x the 10-yr GAAP average 47.2x = 94.4x; P/B is meaningless on negative book equity; P/S 4.94x vs 4.82x 10-yr average. Sanity check passed (exit 0) on 2026-11-08.
